summary.headline: Waaree Renewable Q1 FY27 revenue rose 53.23% YoY to INR924.25 crore, with PAT of INR118.97 crore (+37.7%) and unexecuted order book of INR5,300 crore.
summary.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR924.25 crore, up 53.23% YoY, with EBITDA of INR173.48 crore and PAT of INR118.97 crore. Management executed 888.81 MWp of projects in the quarter and reported an unexecuted order book of INR5,300 crore including T&D, with O&M portfolio at 1.15 GWp. The quarter included completion of a 55% stake acquisition in Associated Power Structures Private Limited (APSPL), a Vadodara T&D EPC and tower maker, which consolidated for about 12 days; management said consolidated margin dipped on lower-margin T&D while standalone EPC margin improved. Management declined to give formal guidance on most items.</overview>

segments.name: Solar EPC (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said standalone EPC EBITDA margin improved QoQ and held in line over the last two years; FY26 EPC EBITDA margin was about 19%. Solar EPC pipeline cited at about 27 GW domestic and about 10-11 GW international.

segments.name: APSPL (T&D, 55% stake)
segments.commentary: Integrated substation and transmission EPC plus fabrication and galvanisation, capacity 108,000 MT per annum, executed over 10,461 circuit km of transmission line. Consolidated margin dilution attributed to this business; T&D pipeline cited at about INR20,000 crore, with typical execution of 18-24 months.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: Order of about 1.5 GWh (reported as roughly 300 MW / 1,400-1,520 MWh across combined orders); unexecuted BESS value about INR200 crore. Margin to be in line with company average at order intake.

segments.name: IPP
segments.commentary: 82 MWp of IPP assets in financials; pipeline of about 198 MWp of small plants (20-25 MW each), for Waaree Renewable Technologies itself.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance given; management said it is not giving margin guidance.

Management indicated it would try to maintain around 15% EBITDA margin for FY27 on a consolidated basis, with APSPL likely not in line with the 19% standalone EPC level; to be updated with Q2 results.
Unexecuted INR5,300 crore order book expected to execute over roughly 12-15 months (or 12-18 months), not within the current fiscal year alone.
Management expects further orders during the remaining nine months of FY27 from the pipeline.
capex_capacity: APSPL acquisition: 55% equity stake completed in the quarter; funded about 75% by debt per management, remainder from internal resources.
IPP pipeline of about 198 MWp of small plants (20-25 MW each); 82 MWp already in financials, some added in Q1.
Execution capacity: management said team can handle 2 GW and 1 GW projects currently and sees no capacity constraint; operates across 7-8 states.
Building capability for data center EPC; no data center order received yet.
demand_pricing: Standalone EPC margin improved QoQ and stable over two years; consolidated margin fell in percentage terms due to T&D consolidation, while absolute EBITDA rose.
Management said it bids only on projects meeting its risk/reward thresholds despite new entrants in solar EPC.
Working capital cycle cited at 60-90 days on progressive billing with customer advances.
Around 30-40% of the solar order book is from group entities, per management, with exact figure to be checked.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2.4 GW order book include BESS, and does the margin gap reflect APSPL consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar EPC order book is about INR2,400 crore and BESS about INR200 crore; standalone margin improved, and the consolidated dip is from lower-margin T&D, with absolute margin rising though percentage fell.

qa_highlights.question: How was the APSPL acquisition financed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 75% debt was used for the acquisition, with the rest self-funded; interest cost will weigh on coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical T&D execution timeline and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: T&D timelines of about 18-24 months, sometimes 9-12 months for shorter lines; T&D pipeline about INR20,000 crore under active pursuit.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash flow after APSPL?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle around 60-90 days on progressive billing; management expects operating cash flow to continue, with funding costs rising.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book comes from group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about 30-40% of the order book is from group entities, and said exact figure would be checked; investors were asked to query via IR.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any margin guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; management said it aims to maintain around 15% EBITDA margin for FY27, with APSPL not in line with the 19% EPC level last year.

risks_watch: Margin dilution from T&D consolidation and rising interest cost on debt-funded APSPL acquisition.
Order book visibility: INR5,300 crore spans 12-18 months, and new order inflow depends on converting a large pipeline.
Related-party share of order book (30-40% per management) and whether such orders are external revenue.
ALMM-II timeline extended to December quarter; impact on order inflow and timelines not quantified.
Management did not answer several questions on BESS per-MW realisation, data center plans, and APSPL standalone financials, pointing investors to segment uploads and IR.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and growth, but evasive on specifics: declined formal guidance, deferred margin and order-flow questions to next quarter, and redirected several queries to IR or other group companies.
key_quotes: We see this acquisition as a step that brings us closer to the grid and power evacuation requirement that go alongside renewable energy capacity addition in the country.
No, we are actually actively looking for any EPC opportunity in the data center.
We are only taking those projects which are really profitable and suits our risk/reward metrics.
